answer: Gate minting behind a memory-hard function with a huge working set. Each identity must fill and randomly traverse gigabytes of RAM to produce its proof, and aggregate memory on one host is a hard ceiling. A single machine can push one proof to its zenith, but stacking a nebula of fakes forces their working sets to contend for the same bounded RAM jetty, thrashing to disk and blowing the deadline. Parallelism buys nothing without buying memory per head, so N identities cost N times the real hardware the farm cannot share.
